questions.question: Describe Durkheim's key ideas and evaluate their relevance to modern society.

points.text: Durkheim: social facts constrain behaviour (laws, norms); collective conscience binds society; anomie occurs when norms break down (explains modern loneliness and rootlessness). Suicide study showed social integration affects suicide rates. Relevance: anomie explains modern problems (social media isolation, community breakdown). Criticism: overstates consensus and understates conflict.

questions.question: Compare Marx and Weber on the causes of capitalism.

points.text: Marx: capitalism arose from class conflict - the bourgeoisie exploited the proletariat. Weber: capitalism arose from cultural/religious factors - the Protestant Ethic created a work ethic that enabled capitalism. Marx emphasises material/economic causes; Weber emphasises cultural/ideational causes. Both contribute: economic structures AND cultural values drive social change.

questions.question: Evaluate which classical sociologist provides the most useful explanation of modern society.

points.text: Durkheim: best for understanding social integration and anomie (relevant to loneliness, mental health). Marx: best for understanding class inequality and exploitation (relevant to wealth gap, zero-hours contracts).
